documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from her office break room. A1c 7.7 from last week, holding. Taking metformin regularly with the auto-refill. Saw GI in December, letter on file: hepatic adenoma, repeat MRI late summer, weight loss. She's trying to cut portions but finds it hard with the store hours. Eye injections continue, spaced out more now she says. No home BP cuff yet.
Plan: no changes. In-person visit early summer with vitals and labs.

documents.title: Ophthalmology follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Visit 03/18/2025.
Diabetic macular edema OU with nonproliferative retinopathy, on intravitreal bevacizumab since 04/2024.
VA cc 20/30 OD, 20/40 OS (from 20/50 and 20/60 at presentation). OCT: marked reduction in central macular thickness both eyes, small residual intraretinal fluid. Fundus: scattered microaneurysms and exudates, fewer than before. No neovascularization.
Injections given today OU. Interval now extended to every 8 to 10 weeks.
Continue glucose and BP control. Copy to PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN follow-up.
Feels fine. Waist still bigger. Hands OK, eyes OK. Saw gyn in the spring per patient, IUD in place, no biopsy needed this time (no letter).
Meds: metformin 500 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, hydroxychloroquine 200 BID (rheum), LNG-IUD.
Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Liver edge palpable, non-tender, as before. No edema. Feet normal, monofilament intact.
A/P: continue current regimen. GI MRI due August, she has it scheduled. Labs today. Physical in the fall.
Addendum: A1c 7.8. Creatinine 1.08. AST 46, ALT 70, mildly up as GI has seen; they are following.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: Indication: surveillance of known hepatic adenoma. Comparison 11/25/2024. Hepatomegaly, unchanged. The right hepatic lobe lesion measures 3.9 x 3.4 cm (previously 3.8 x 3.4 cm), with the same intralesional fat and arterial enhancement pattern, no washout. No hemorrhage. No new hepatic lesions. Vessels patent. Remaining upper abdominal organs unremarkable. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Stable 3.9 cm hepatic adenoma without hemorrhage or new lesion.

documents.title: Gastroenterology follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology and hepatology group
Follow-up visit 08/13/2025

Ms. Thompson returns for her liver adenoma. Her waist has kept growing even though she has been dieting. No abdominal pain. No alcohol.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. NKDA.
Exam: BMI 34. Mild hepatomegaly. No jaundice, no spider angiomata, no ascites.
Labs today: fasting glucose 162, A1c 7.8, AST 48, ALT 82, total cholesterol 220, HDL 35, triglycerides 250.
MRI 08/04/2025: adenoma 3.9 cm, essentially unchanged, no bleeding.
Assessment: stable hepatocellular adenoma under 5 cm. Transaminases somewhat higher than in December.
Plan: continue weight loss efforts, avoid estrogen. Yearly MRI. Recheck liver tests with her PCP. Return after next MRI.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu L arm and Moderna 2025-26 R arm. No issues. GI follow-up letter from August arrived 9/30 and is in the chart for PCP; she asked if her liver numbers were bad, told her the doctor will go over it at the physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
55 y/o for physical.
No new complaints. Energy OK. No chest pain or breathing trouble. Eyes: injections every couple of months, vision good enough to drive. Hands: occasional morning stiffness, rheum every 6 months (no letters since Feb 2024). Gyn yearly per patient.
GI letter (8/13) reviewed: adenoma stable 3.9 cm, yearly MRI, ALT 82 there.
Meds: metformin 500 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, hydroxychloroquine 200 BID, LNG-IUD.
SH: 1 ppd. No alcohol. Two jobs.

Exam: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, liver edge palpable as before, non-tender. No edema. Feet: intact, pulses present, monofilament normal. Joints without active synovitis.

A/P
1. T2DM with macular edema: continue metformin; ophthalmology injections ongoing.
2. HTN: continue lisinopril 20.
3. Lipids: continue atorvastatin 20.
4. Hepatic adenoma: GI surveillance, MRI next summer.
5. RA: rheum managing hydroxychloroquine.
6. Endometrial hyperplasia: gyn surveillance with IUD.
7. Tobacco: still 1 ppd; advised quitting.
8. HM: mammogram and LDCT ordered. Flu/COVID done 10/14.
Addendum 11/19: creatinine 1.2, eGFR now below 60 for the first time (previous creatinine about 1.0-1.1). Will repeat at next visit before calling it anything. A1c 7.9. AST/ALT 47/76, in line with GI's. Hgb 12.7.

reports.text: Screening tomosynthesis compared with prior studies back to 2021. Scattered fibroglandular density. No mass, suspicious calcification or architectural distortion.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Annual screening, comparison 12/10/2024. No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. Heart size within normal limits. No effusion. Known hepatomegaly partly imaged.

conditions.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

medications.reason: held in the ED for creatinine 1.8

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

reports.text: Sinus rhythm at 88 bpm. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No acute ST-segment elevation or depression.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm without acute ischemic changes.

reports.text: Portable AP chest. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Pulmonary vascular congestion with indistinct vessels. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax. No large effusion.

Technically adequate study. Left ventricle normal in size with concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Global systolic function reduced, ejection fraction estimated 40% by biplane method. Right ventricle normal size and function. Atria normal size. Valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal caliber.
reports.conclusion: Left ventricular hypertrophy with reduced ejection fraction, LVEF 40%.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional emergency department, received by fax 06/24/2026.
Arrived 06/10/2026 15:40. Placed in observation; discharged 06/11/2026.

CC: getting more tired and short of breath.
HPI: 56-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia and prior iron deficiency anemia. Fatigue and breathlessness with exertion have built up over about six months and became much worse this week; she could not finish a shift. Unintentionally lost about 15 pounds over the same six months. No chest pain.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin 20 mg. NKDA. Smokes. No alcohol.
Social: works two jobs, little time to exercise, mostly processed food because it is cheaper and closer to home.

Exam: BP 142/90, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 94% on room air, BMI 32. Bibasilar crackles. Heart regular. 1+ pitting edema both lower legs.

Results: A1c 8.2, fasting glucose 176 (next morning), creatinine 1.8 (baseline 1.2), BNP 580. Urinalysis 2+ protein, no glucose or ketones. High-sensitivity troponin 6 then 7, not elevated. ECG sinus rhythm, no acute changes. CXR: cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion. Echo (6/11): LVH, EF 40%.

Course: furosemide 40 mg IV once with good urine output; breathing easier overnight, SpO2 97% on room air by morning.

Diagnosis: new heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Disposition: home. Furosemide 20 mg by mouth daily. Lisinopril held until kidney function rechecked. Other medications unchanged. Daily weights, 2 g sodium. See primary care within 1-2 weeks for BMP and medication review; outpatient cardiology referral recommended.

documents.title: I was in the ER
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I was in the ER Wednesday and stayed overnight. They said my heart isn't pumping right and gave me a water pill. They stopped my lisinopril. They told me to see you in a week or two. Breathing is better.

documents.title: RE: I was in the ER
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sorry to hear that, glad you're breathing easier. I booked you with the doctor on Friday 6/26 at 4:20 and we're requesting the ER records. Weigh yourself every morning and write it down. If you gain more than 3 pounds in a day or 5 in a week, or get short of breath lying flat, call us or go back to the ER.

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Seen in the ED 6/10 with observation overnight (record received 6/24): new heart failure, EF 40% with LVH on echo, BNP 580, creatinine 1.8 against a 1.2 baseline, CXR with congestion. Sent home on furosemide 20 daily with lisinopril held. Since then breathing is much better, can do the office stairs slowly, ankles less puffy, sleeping flat. Home weights trending down. No chest pain, no palpitations, no lightheadedness. She also notes she had lost about 15 pounds over the six months before the ED without trying; appetite has been so-so.
Meds now: furosemide 20 daily, metformin 500 BID, atorvastatin 20, hydroxychloroquine 200 BID (rheum), LNG-IUD. Lisinopril on hold.
SH: still smoking about a pack a day.

O: BP 132/82. Weight as charted, a little lower than in the ED. Not in distress, speaking full sentences. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no gallop or murmur. Lungs clear at the bases today. Trace ankle edema. Liver edge palpable as before.

A/P
1. HFrEF, new, EF 40% with LVH; likely hypertensive/diabetic but needs a cardiology workup. Euvolemic today. Continue furosemide 20 daily. Restart ACE inhibitor at lisinopril 10 mg daily if today's creatinine allows; start metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily. Cardiology referral placed for further therapy and evaluation. Daily weights, sodium limit, call for gain of 3 lb/day or 5 lb/week.
2. Kidney function: BMP today and again in 2 weeks after the restart.
3. Weight loss: CBC and TSH today; will review with cardiology input and at follow-up.
4. T2DM: A1c 8.2 in ED. Continue metformin for now pending kidney function.
5. Tobacco: quitting matters more than ever with her heart; she'll think about a quit date and call.
6. Hepatic adenoma: MRI due around August per GI.
RTC 4-6 weeks.
Addendum 19:50: creatinine 1.3. OK to restart lisinopril at 10 mg as planned; message sent.

documents.title: Your labs from yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning. Kidney number is 1.3, much better than the 1.8 in the ER, so please start the lisinopril 10 mg (new prescription at your pharmacy) along with the metoprolol. Blood count and thyroid are normal. Lab again in about 2 weeks, order is in. Keep logging your weights.

documents.title: RE: Your labs from yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thank you. Picked up both. Weight this morning 195.

documents.title: Lab result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Kidney function steady at 1.3 and potassium 4.7 on the lisinopril. No changes. Has cardiology called you with a date yet? If not, let us know and we'll follow up on the referral.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request for furosemide 20 mg from the pharmacy; the ER prescription was a 30-day supply. Sent 90 days per PCP. Metoprolol and lisinopril filled 6/27 with refills.
